title: Vendor Logging and Forensics Cooperation Template
content:
Purpose:
This template establishes minimum contractual obligations for vendors providing services to Redwood Inference regarding system logging, log integrity, forensic cooperation, evidence preservation, and related operational and legal coordination. It is intended to be attached to or incorporated into a Master Services Agreement (MSA) or Data Processing Agreement (DPA) when vendor systems generate or process telemetry, application logs, security events, or other artifacts that may be relevant to security investigations, compliance audits, or legal proceedings.

Scope:
Applies to all vendors ("Supplier") that host, process, transport, or otherwise have access to logs, telemetry, or system artifacts from services used by Redwood Inference ("Customer"). This template covers production and non-production environments when those environments affect Customer data, authentication flows, or critical service availability.

Definitions:
- "Logs": Recorded events, traces, metrics, audit records, access records, or any digital artifacts that capture system, application, or user activity.
- "Forensic Evidence": A subset of Logs preserved and handled according to chain-of-custody practices for investigation or legal use.
- "Preservation Hold": A written directive from Customer requiring Supplier to preserve specified Logs and artifacts.
- "Authorized Request": A substantiated request from Customer security, legal, or its designated agents for access to or transfer of Forensic Evidence.

1. Logging and Log Quality Requirements
1.1. Standard Logging Coverage: Supplier shall record, at minimum, the following event classes for systems processing Customer activity: authentication events (success/failure), administrative actions, API requests and responses (including request IDs and timestamps), configuration changes, container/VM lifecycle events, and system errors that impact availability or data integrity.
1.2. Structured and Correlated Logs: Logs shall be structured (JSON, protobuf, or equivalent) where practicable, include UTC timestamps (ISO 8601), a correlation identifier for request tracing, system/component identifiers, and a log level.
1.3. Clock Synchronization: Supplier shall maintain synchronized system clocks (NTP or equivalent) with maximum clock skew of 2 seconds for systems producing forensic-grade logs.

2. Retention and Indexing
2.1. Minimum Retention: Supplier shall retain security-relevant logs for a minimum of 13 months unless otherwise agreed in writing or required by applicable law. Operational metrics and high-volume debug traces may be retained for shorter durations subject to mutual agreement.
2.2. Indexed Storage: Security and access logs shall be indexed and queryable by timestamp, correlation ID, affected resource, and user identifier. Indexing must support export of query results in machine-readable formats.

3. Integrity, Anti-Tamper Controls, and Backup
3.1. Tamper Detection: Supplier shall implement mechanisms to detect and alert on log tampering or deletion attempts (immutable append-only stores, WORM storage, cryptographic signing, or equivalent).
3.2. Backup and Redundancy: Forensic-grade logs shall be replicated to a separate availability boundary (different cluster/region/account) with backups retained for the required retention window.
3.3. Access Controls: Access to raw logs and forensic repositories must be restricted by role-based access control (RBAC), require multi-factor authentication for administrative roles, and record all access to log archives.

4. Preservation and Chain of Custody
4.1. Preservation Hold: Upon receipt of a Preservation Hold from Customer, Supplier shall preserve the specified Logs and artifacts, suspend any automatic deletion or retention policies affecting those items, and confirm preservation within 24 hours.
4.2. Chain of Custody Documentation: Supplier shall maintain a chain-of-custody record for preserved artifacts, including source, custody transfers, timestamps, personnel actions, and checksums/hashes demonstrating integrity. These records must be exportable and provided to Customer on request.
4.3. Export Formats: Forensic Evidence exports shall be provided in commonly accepted formats (e.g., gzipped JSON/NDJSON, PCAP for network captures, signed checksum manifest) with accompanying metadata describing collection time window, collection method, and applied filters.

5. Access and Evidence Transfer
5.1. Authorized Access: Supplier shall provide secure, auditable access to preserved Forensic Evidence to Customer and Customer-designated investigators within 48 hours of an Authorized Request, faster if operationally feasible.
5.2. Secure Transfer: Evidence transfers must use encrypted channels (TLS 1.2+), with mutual authentication where possible. When large volumes or physical media transfers are necessary, Supplier and Customer shall agree on secure courier, encryption at rest, and verification steps prior to ingestion.

6. Cooperation, Investigation Support, and Timeframes
6.1. Incident Support: Supplier will designate a technical point of contact available for incident investigations and will provide reasonable engineering support (log queries, runbooks, reconstruction of events) during a declared incident. Initial technical contact response time shall be within 2 business hours for Severity 1 incidents and 8 business hours for lower severities.
6.2. Technical Reports: Following an investigation, Supplier shall provide a written incident summary identifying impacted services, timeline of events, actions taken, root cause analysis (if known), and evidence locations within 10 business days or a mutually agreed timeline.
6.3. Preservation Duration Extension: If an investigation is ongoing, Customer may request extensions to retention beyond the minimum retention period; Supplier shall grant reasonable extensions for the duration of the investigation and any related legal holds.

7. Costs and Reasonable Fees
7.1. Routine Access: Routine access to logs for operational troubleshooting is considered part of the contracted service.
7.2. Extraordinary Forensic Work: Supplier may charge reasonable, documented fees for extraordinary forensic services (e.g., custom log reprocessing, off-hours support, physical media handling). Any such fees must be estimated in advance and approved by Customer in writing.

8. Confidentiality, Use Restrictions, and Data Minimization
8.1. Use Limitation: Supplier may use preserved Forensic Evidence solely to comply with the obligations in this agreement, except where lawful disclosure is required. Supplier shall not use or disclose Customer-specific evidence for product development, analytics, or other commercial purposes without Customers prior written consent.
8.2. Minimization: To the extent possible consistent with forensic goals, Supplier shall minimize exposure of unrelated Customer data in evidence exports (redaction or field filtering) and document any data elements that cannot be redacted.

9. Regulatory and Law Enforcement Requests
9.1. Notice and Cooperation: To the extent permitted by law, Supplier shall notify Customer promptly (and in any case within 48 hours) of any third-party or law enforcement request seeking Customer logs or Forensic Evidence and cooperate in seeking protective measures. Supplier will consult Customer prior to producing evidence when permitted.

10. Audit Rights and Validation
10.1. Self-Attestation: Supplier shall provide an annual self-attestation of compliance with the logging and preservation controls described herein and produce supporting artifacts on request.
10.2. Third-Party Audit: Customer may request a third-party assessment of Suppliers log integrity and preservation controls at Customers expense; Supplier shall reasonably cooperate and provide access to auditors under mutually agreed scope and confidentiality terms.

11. Dispute Resolution and Limitation of Liability
11.1. Escalation Path: Parties shall designate primary and secondary security contacts and follow the contact and escalation procedures described in the MSA.
11.2. Liability for Failure to Preserve: If Supplier negligently fails to preserve or provide Forensic Evidence in breach of this addendum and such failure causes direct, provable harm to Customer, Suppliers liability for that failure shall be subject to the liability provisions in the MSA but may include reasonable remediation costs.

12. Termination and Survivability
12.1. Survivability: The obligations in this addendum regarding preservation, confidentiality, access to evidence, and auditability shall survive termination of the underlying MSA for a period of at least 18 months or where longer retention is required by law.

13. Miscellaneous
13.1. Local Laws: Where local law imposes stricter log retention, preservation, or disclosure obligations, Supplier shall comply with the stricter standard and shall notify Customer promptly of any conflict.
13.2. Amendments: Any deviation from the minimum standards in this template must be documented and agreed in writing by both parties.

Sample Preservation Hold Process (operational steps):
1) Customer issues Preservation Hold specifying timeframe, data classes, correlation IDs, and contact info.
2) Supplier acknowledges within 24 hours and confirms systems/indices affected.
3) Supplier applies hold, creates chain-of-custody folder, and captures checksums.
4) Supplier confirms preservation and provides export ETA or provides immediate access for critical items.
5) Customer retrieves evidence and invoices for any pre-approved extraordinary fees.

Signatures:

Notes and negotiation points (non-exhaustive):
- Consider narrowing 13-month retention where log volume or privacy concerns make this impractical; alternatively negotiate tiered retention for high-value security logs.
- Technical appendix can be attached listing log schemas, retention endpoints, and available query tools.
- Define escalation contacts and on-call expectations for Severity 1 incidents in the MSA or SOW.
- Where Supplier cannot provide raw logs (managed service black-box), negotiate access to reconstructed telemetry and certified attestations of events.

End of template.
